title: Sizing summary: Elasticsearch 9.5.5, logsdb vs logsdb_columnar vs TSDS

how_to_read.raw_bytes: Raw NDJSON bytes of the generated documents (bulk action lines excluded). This is the 100 GiB reference.
how_to_read.primary_store_bytes: Primary shard store size after refresh and force-merge to one segment per shard.
how_to_read.structures: On-disk structures from the index disk usage API. A field's bytes are its share of each structure.
how_to_read.columnar_saving_percent: How much smaller logsdb_columnar is than logsdb, as a percentage of the logsdb size.
how_to_read.original_copy: logsdb keeps a copy of match_only_text values (`<field>._original`) for synthetic _source. Columnar stores the text in doc values instead.

metrics_tsds.single_mode_only: TSDS has no columnar counterpart; shown for completeness
metrics_tsds.store_note: The verification report recorded 1903391531 bytes (1.77 GiB); re-measurement gives 1166027740 bytes. See store_reconciliation.

store_reconciliation.method: Current store size from index disk usage (store_size_in_bytes). The same values were confirmed by _stats after a flush, and for the metrics index also after a second force-merge.
store_reconciliation.open_question: The metrics store recorded by verify_es.py (22 Oct) is 1,903,391,531 bytes. It cannot be reproduced: the current store is 1,166,027,740 bytes and stays the same after flush and force-merge. The cause is not determined.
